thread.title: Malaysia Bourse May Halt Losing Streak

author: rttnews.com
title: Malaysia Bourse May Halt Losing Streak
text:
The Malaysia stock market has finished lower in three straight sessions, giving away more than 15 points or 0.9 percent along the way. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now rests just beneath the 1,685-point plateau although it may stop the bleeding on Thursday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is broadly positive on an improved outlook for interest rates and a spike in crude oil prices. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are predicted to follow suit.
The KLCI finished modestly lower on Wednesday following losses from the financial shares and plantation stocks.
For the day, the index sank 6.30 points or 0.37 percent to finish at 1,684.11 after trading between 1,681.57 and 1,691.23. Volume was 1.9 billion shares worth 1.7 billion ringgit. There were 424 decliners and 320 gainers.
Among the actives, Tenaga Nasional plummeted 2.67 percent, while Sime Darby surged 2.26 percent, Axiata Group soared 2.02 percent, Top Glove plunged 1.83 percent, Petronas Chemicals tumbled 1.42 percent, Hartalega Holdings skidded 1.25 percent, Digi.com dropped 1.08 percent, Maybank retreated 0.93 percent, RHB Capital declined 0.91 percent, IHH Healthcare jumped 0.54 percent, Kuala Lumpur Kepong shed 0.49 percent, IOI Corporation lost 0.43 percent, Dialog Group fell 0.33 percent, Genting and Hong Leong Bank both advanced 0.29 percent, CIMB Group eased 0.18 percent and Genting Malaysia, Press Metal and Hong Leong Financial were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is firm in response to the Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement, which sent the major averages to nearly two-month closing highs.
The Dow added 434.90 points or 1.77 while the NASDAQ surged 154.79 points or 2.20 rose 41.05 points or 1.55 percent to 2,681.05.
Stocks accelerated to the upside after the Fed
Positive sentiment was also generated by solid earnings news from companies like Boeing (BA) and Apple (AAPL).
 West Texas Intermediate Crude oil futures barrel.
Closer to home, Malaysia will release December data for producer prices later today; in November, prices were down 2.8 percent on month and 2.9 percent on year.
